markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Repeated textual agreement can distinguish specific interests from broad resemblance. Agreement must span distinct items so duplicate purchases cannot manufacture support. (2) A semantic residual can expose identifiable connections to history. Similarity alone cannot establish compatibility or added capability. (3) Multi-negative training directly challenges ranking errors. Electronics’ 16.98% sampled-pair error motivates testing it, but does not predict validation improvement.

**Related-work insights.** (1) gSASRec [1] motivates reconsidering sampled BCE calibration. Sampling comparisons [2] caution that harder negatives are not universally better. (2) FSASA [3] separates recent and global preference signals. This motivates recency weighting without requiring another transformer. (3) MERLIN [4] distinguishes directional associations from semantic resemblance. Its relationship supervision is unavailable here, so behavioral transitions remain predictive evidence only.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Unresolved limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking objective | gBCE; sampling comparisons [1,2] | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Sampled training errors need not track HR@10 |
| Current, specific intent | Local/global fusion [3] | Recent, repeated semantic support | New interests may lack repetition |
| Useful successors | Asymmetric associations [4] | Shrunk directed-transition residual | Transitions do not prove compatibility |

### Candidate assessment

Scores are hypotheses, not experimental results. O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell gives score and positive/negative rationale.

| Idea | O | P | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Uniform multi-negative softmax [1,2] | 2; clear baseline / established | 7; reusable / limited mechanism | 3; sharper ranking / no intent signal | 8; challenges errors / surrogate only | 2; localized / masking required |
| B: Recency-and-repeat semantic residual [3] | 5; support calibration / familiar components | 8; interpretable / sparse text | 8; specificity and freshness / compatibility unresolved | 7; combined-score training / transfer uncertain | 4; fixed text features / inference integration |
| C: Directed-transition residual [4] | 4; directional evidence / established approach | 7; successor modeling / sparse edges | 7; task continuity / accidental transitions | 6; extra discriminative signal / popularity confounding | 5; sparse counts / prefix leakage risk |

### Selected idea: B

At 10% progress, simplify the initial learned-text proposal: use fixed TF–IDF features from permitted titles/descriptions and one bounded residual coefficient per dataset. Explicit recency addresses outdated interests; repeated, specific textual support addresses broad associations and unexplained recommendations. Uniform multi-negative softmax targets observed positive–negative ranking errors, particularly in Electronics.

```text
For each causal training prefix:
  deduplicate recent item IDs, keeping their latest occurrence
  weight each by recency × agreement with other distinct recent items
  pool normalized TF–IDF vectors; return zero for unsupported histories
  score = SASRec score + bounded_alpha × cosine(pool, candidate_text)
  optimize uniform multi-negative softmax on combined scores
```

Use continuous agreement and shrink low-support pools. Compare baseline, loss-only, and residual variants under unchanged seeds, splits, routing, and pinned macro validation HR@10. Fit vocabulary only on training-observed item metadata. Preserve the diagnosis interface, adapt probes to combined scores, and export identical pooling/scoring through the predictor writer. No gains or compatibility guarantees are claimed.

idea.description: Add a bounded semantic residual to per-dataset SASRec using recency-weighted, repeated textual support across distinct historical items. Use fixed TF–IDF features initially and train the combined scorer with uniform multi-negative sampled softmax.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations and outdated interests as separate failures. Repeated textual support targets specificity, while recency weighting reduces stale influence. The combined ranking objective addresses the observed sampled-pair errors, without treating those training diagnostics as validation evidence.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain all four datasets and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts only beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Build sparse TF–IDF from permitted titles/descriptions for training-observed items; missing or unseen vocabulary yields zero features. Keep pooling causal at every training position. Count support across distinct nonpadding item IDs, excluding self-agreement; combine it with exponential event-recency weighting. Shrink the pooled vector using total support, since normalization alone would remove confidence magnitude. Initialize the bounded nonnegative residual coefficient at zero and tune its cap using validation. Sample uniform negatives from eligible items, excluding padding, the target, and observed training positives; use no held-out interactions for filtering. Do not add an unverified logQ correction. Compare unchanged SASRec, loss-only, and the residual under the common macro validation HR@10 and shared GPU budget. Persist vocabulary, IDF, item features, pooling parameters, architecture configuration, and weights; update the predictor writer to reproduce combined scores in working/predict.py. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Keep view.model as the actual trained module and expose item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data through the compatibility adapter; carry semantic prefix features alongside SASRec features so diagnostic margins use deployed scores. Report embedding alignment only as a descriptive statistic. No reviews, ratings, categories, prices, stores, simulator traits, pretrained weights, or hidden test data are required.
idea.pseudocode:
fit TFIDF on permitted metadata for training-observed items
for each dataset, each training batch:
    h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
    for each valid causal prefix:
        ids = latest_occurrence_unique(prefix[-K:])
        z = normalized_sparse_TFIDF(ids)
        agreement[j] = mean cosine(z[j], z[k]) over k != j
        weights = exp(-event_age / tau) * agreement
        pool = weighted_mean(z, weights)
        confidence = sum(weights) / (sum(weights) + shrinkage)
        semantic_state = confidence * normalize(pool), or zero
    candidates = positive plus M eligible uniform negatives
    scores = ID_scores(h, candidates) + bounded_alpha * semantic_state_dot_item_text
    loss = cross_entropy(scores, positive_index)
    update model and residual coefficient
select controlled variant using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10
export architecture, weights, TFIDF artifacts, and matching predictor writer

originality.positive: Combines distinct-item support, recency, and bounded semantic evidence in a small, interpretable extension.
originality.negative: Semantic residuals and local/global preference weighting are established components; novelty is primarily their calibration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a feasible foundation for studying when semantic evidence reflects persistent current interests across different product domains.
future_potential.negative: Repeated textual similarity can suppress emerging interests and cannot establish product compatibility or complementarity.

code_difficulty.positive: Fixed sparse text features avoid an additional learned encoder and auxiliary training objective.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal prefix pooling, confidence shrinkage, diagnostic adaptation, and predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)
contributions: Attributes part of SASRec overconfidence to sampled BCE and proposes generalized BCE.
Motivates an objective-only control before adding architecture.
limitations: Does not establish gains under this pinned four-category evaluation.
Objective calibration alone does not explicitly address stale interests or broad semantic associations.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024): negative-sampling comparisons
contributions: Compares uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed, and adaptive negative sampling.
Motivates uniform multi-negative training as an essential control.
limitations: Sampling effectiveness and popularity effects depend on the dataset.
Harder negatives cannot be assumed to improve the host's fixed-candidate HR@10.

related_work.title: FSASA (2024)
contributions: Combines global SASRec preference with a session-aware local branch and GRU-based weighting.
Motivates distinguishing recent intent from older preference.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed repeated-support semantic residual.
The supplied evidence establishes no improvement on this exact benchmark.

related_work.title: MERLIN (CIKM 2024)
contributions: Models asymmetric item associations using separate source and destination representations.
Motivates distinguishing resemblance from directional purchase usefulness.
limitations: Its association supervision cannot be assumed available from this task's interaction histories.
Semantic agreement does not recover verified complementarity or compatibility labels.
